agency_full: European Space Agency (lead) — NASA (RIME radar antenna + UVS spectrometer) + JAXA (PEP-Hi components) + ISA (Italian Space Agency 3GM radio science + JANUS imager)
payload: 6000 kg wet (2900 kg dry) — largest interplanetary spacecraft Europe has ever built. 10 instruments: JANUS (visible), MAJIS (IR), UVS, SWI (sub-mm), GALA (laser altimeter), RIME (radar sounder, NASA), J-MAG (mag), PEP (particle), RPWI (plasma waves), 3GM (radio science). 85 m² solar arrays sized for ~5.5 AU operation.
delta_v: ~3.0 km/s (gravity-assist sequence + Jupiter orbit insertion + Ganymede orbit insertion)
credit: © ESA / Airbus / instrument PIs. JUICE — JUpiter ICy moons Explorer — launched 2023-04-14 from Kourou as ESA's flagship L-class outer-system mission. The 8-year cruise is one of the most complex gravity-assist sequences ever attempted: a unique Lunar-Earth Gravity Assist (LEGA) on 2024-08-19 (first such manoeuvre ever performed), Venus 2025-08-31, Earth 2026-09-29, Earth 2029-01-18, with each pass building ΔV toward Jupiter arrival 2031-07-21. After Jupiter orbit insertion JUICE will conduct 35 close flybys of Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto over 3.5 years before manoeuvring into a dedicated Ganymede orbit on 2034-12-31 — the first spacecraft ever to orbit a moon of another planet. Primary science questions: Is there a subsurface ocean at Ganymede? What is the composition + thickness of Europa's ice shell? How do the Jovian magnetic environment + ice-shell tides interact across the three icy moons? Planned end of mission 2035 by impact on Ganymede.

events.label: Launch — Ariane 5 ECA
events.description: Kourou, French Guiana, 2023-04-14. ESA's first L-class mission and the first European spacecraft to Jupiter. Juice (JUpiter ICy moons Explorer) targets the three Galilean ice moons — Ganymede, Callisto, Europa — to test whether their subsurface oceans could be habitable.

events.label: Earth + Moon — first-ever lunar gravity assist
events.description: August 2024. The first spacecraft to use a Moon flyby (closest approach 700 km) followed by an Earth flyby (closest approach 6,800 km) within 24 hours — a coupled double assist that ESA engineers designed to bend Juice's trajectory toward Venus while saving ~100 m/s of ∆v versus a pure Earth-only flyby.

events.label: Venus — gravity assist
events.description: August 2025. Closest approach ~9,000 km from Venus. The encounter raises Juice's aphelion enough that two more Earth assists in 2026 + 2029 will reach Jupiter. The Venus thermal environment is the hottest the spacecraft will face — passive thermal control was designed around this pass.

events.label: Earth #2 — gravity assist
events.description: September 2026. Adds energy for the third leg of the cruise to Jupiter.

events.label: Earth #3 — gravity assist
events.description: January 2029. Final gravity assist before the direct trajectory to Jupiter — adds the last ~5 km/s needed for the long cruise to arrival in 2031.

events.label: Jupiter orbit insertion
events.description: Planned 2031-07. Multi-month capture burn into Jupiter orbit. After 35 Jupiter orbits with Europa + Callisto + Ganymede flybys, Juice will become the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's (Ganymede) in 2034 — settling into a 5,000 km circular orbit to map the largest moon in the solar system.
